question: A Power has a lower threshold requiring 2 Water and a higher threshold requiring 3 Water. Its Spirit has 3 Water. May the Spirit resolve that Power as if it had only 2 Water, getting the lower threshold but not the higher one? May another Power still check the Spirit's actual 3 Water later this turn? Assume no instruction gains or loses Elements.
answer: Yes to both. The Spirit may resolve the first Power as if it had fewer Elements, consistently for that entire Power, and must resolve the base effect plus all thresholds met by that assumed set. The hypothetical reduction does not spend or remove actual Elements, so another Power may still use the actual 3 Water. It is not permission to select or skip individual threshold instructions independently.

exact_source_refs.label: CORE p17 Elemental Thresholds: may always resolve a Power as if fewer Elements; Elements not used up
FAQ Core .bu6od0c footnote 1: explicitly may activate only lower innate level; entire-Power consistency

new_coverage: Q73 asks whether a higher threshold can be used while omitting a lower threshold whose requirements are also met. The answer is no under both the correct optional-reduction rule and the incorrect rule that all actually met thresholds are always compulsory. The proposed positive case distinguishes those rules: it requests the explicitly published permission to omit a higher level by consistently assuming fewer Elements. This is a source-defined allowed branch, not merely reversing the answer to Q73 or substituting a different number.
coverage_credit_limit: The new coverage is the positive, Power-local permission to assume fewer Elements. Ordinary reuse of unspent actual Elements across Powers is already within Q15; the second-Power clause checks that the voluntary assumption has not been mistaken for a real global Element loss and should not be counted as a separate discovery.
